reviews.review: The game is fun with good graphics and mechanics. BUT it is ridiculous that you must pay for more levels. The game is expensive as is, but They really want to suck you dry. Feels like a rip-off.

It's hard to give the game the review that truly encapsulates everything that needs to be said. For starters, it truly is a shame the dev team gave up on this so soon in its history given the lasting success of L4D2 and the community that kept it alive and well with truly creative modding. Having said that, I am happy with the vanilla game and where it stands considering that the last update it received will truly be its last update in its lifetime. Others may disagree with me on this but I enjoy the campaign from start to finish and the extra additions. I think its very cool that each one of my friends has a specific character that truly accentuates the build they want to make via the card system, myself included. And that the fine tuning difficulty of Trial of the Worm lets us have just the right amount of challenge that keeps us playing. Overall, I have fun while playing this game but only if there a team of three other people willing to run it with me, which I almost always have, fortunately. I also greatly enjoy the ridden hives and the rare double hive encounters for extra totems. There's just something about deep diving into the rotten hellscape and walking out with legendary guns that feels fun every time.

If you have several friends who enjoy zombie shooters and need to kill a few hours this is a great game and I believe it's worth at least the sale price of 12 bucks. If you're a solo player or struggle to consistently get your friends away from whatever lame-skin royale they're playing, this is not worth it. 

For the numerous and depressing downsides, I'll start with the fact they couldn't even be bothered to have holiday themes on autopilot. For one year they had festive themes and music changes to the campsite, even double skull totem weekends. Not anymore. And while I do enjoy the numerous characters to choose from and the buffs they provide, only after playing for two years did I hear a SINGLE realistic dialogue that remotely resembled an actual conversation between humans. And that was literally yesterday. The one liners are bad, the dialogue is bad, but not unbearable and is easy to tune out except for Tala. If nothing else I wish they would remove every one of her voice lines from the game including her campaign arc. 

TL;DR
It's not the best game in the world and it's not the worst game in the world. If you've got several friends who want to kill an afternoon this is a great way to do that. But only when it's on sale.
